jobs.title: Director of Operations, Slate Development
jobs.location: US - Culver City, California, United States; US - United States
jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Director, Slate Operations to join our Slate Development Group team in the US remotely or in Culver City on a flexible hybrid model.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

Slate Operations keeps Scopely's game development slate moving. We oversee execution and cross-functional alignment across the games in development — connecting game teams and central teams so decisions get made once and stick, running the cadence that keeps everyone aligned, and clearing the path so teams can build.

What You'll Do:

We're looking for a Director, Slate Operations to own this end to end. There are two sides to it: keeping the Group running as an organization — its cadence, process, and the day-to-day support the Game Board, Head of Slate Development and leadership team rely on — and running program management for the Game Development Framework (GDF) so games move cleanly from concept to launch. You'll sit inside the Slate Development Group but work with every part of Scopely: game teams, divisional leadership, finance, strategy, and corporate development.

- Be the operational point of contact for specific in-development games — running the GDF cadence and connecting game and central teams so decisions get made once and aren't re-litigated. The main goal is to be the end to end steward for game teams in the game development framework.

- Deliver operational excellence within our internal team, shaping our service model, priorities, and ways of working. Evolve our capabilities as needs change.

- Drive the cross-slate operating model so independent game teams reuse what already works instead of rebuilding it.

- Bring structure to consequential decisions — organize the inputs, assumptions, and trade-offs early so the owners and the room can reach real alignment before committing.

- Own a capstone project — one meaty area you drive end to end, for example: evolving the GDF, owning launch readiness, or operationalizing central partnerships, depending on where the need is.

- Keep investment decisions well-informed — track progress across games at different stages, and surface Greenlight Case, budget, staffing, and dependency status so leadership can challenge and decide.

- Unblock teams through the development cycle, especially at launch readiness, by clearing operational issues with central partners (legal, IT, procurement, finance, logistics) so teams stay focused on the game. Partner with marketing, strategy, and divisional leadership so launches go out clean.

- Give teams operational support — production perspective, process, facilitation, and help navigating the GDF.

- Operationalize playtests and validation — help build and run research, playtest, and validation plans, and package the findings so vertical owners and leaders can form the recommendation.

- Utilize the latest AI technologies to keep information flowing — the dashboards, status, and key dates people need to see, without the overhead.

What We’re Looking For:

- Bachelor's degree, MBA a plus — or the equivalent in experience.

- 10+ years in program/project management across tech and direct-to-consumer businesses, at least 5 of them in games, working within or alongside a development team.

- You know how games get made and sold — development, publishing, platforms, business models. You don't need to have shipped one yourself, but you get what game teams are up against.

- You've supported senior execs in a fast-moving environment and you like the pace — taking initiative, juggling priorities, switching gears without losing the thread.

- You can run a lot of projects at once, ideally a mix of R&D and live.

- You're comfortable in ambiguity and good at creating clarity for other people. You make sound calls in the company's interest and know when to escalate.

- You can hold your own with P&Ls and free-to-play KPIs.

- You spot the process that's slowing people down and fix it — and you'll push back and start the right debate when it matters.

- You build trust with all kinds of people at every level and don't flinch at the hard conversations — with the presence to grow into a partner to senior game leaders over time.

- You write clearly and fast, and you can build a strong deck with cross-functional input.

- Detail and organization come naturally to you.

- Low ego, business outcomes first, open to feedback — and genuinely curious about every part of the business.

- You play games and care about the industry.

For candidates in CA, CO, NJ, NY, and WA, the annual salary range is provided below. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for equity, bonuses, and a comprehensive benefits package, including healthcare benefits, retirement benefits, pet insurance, paid holidays, paid Scopely free days, and unlimited paid time off. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

CA, CO, NJ, NY, and WA Annual Salary Range
$139,400 — $205,000 USD

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

jobs.description:

MARVEL Strike Force is Scopely's squad-based Hero Collector RPG, housing heroes and villains across the Marvel Universe.

What You Will Do

You will be the operational bridge between Live Ops strategy and high-quality in-game execution. You will gather requirements from the events and monetization teams, translate them into executable plans and configurable designs, and manage work across our Live Ops implementation partner. The role is accountable not only for accurate configuration, but also for ensuring that offers, events, milestones, and rewards remain complementary to the broader strategy and value proposition.

- Translate Strategy into Execution: Turn high-level designs for offers, events, milestones, rewards, and other Live Ops components into clear Jira tickets, configuration specifications, acceptance criteria, and implementation plans

- Manage the Implementation Partner: Prioritize, delegate, and track work across our Live Ops implementation partner, ensuring that owners, dependencies, timing, and escalation paths are clear

- Own Execution Readiness: Maintain a reliable view of upcoming launches, confirm that requirements and assets are complete, and drive issues to resolution before they create player-facing or business risk

- Provide Strategic and Value Quality Assurance: Review configured content for technical accuracy, player value, internal consistency, and alignment with the intended engagement and monetization strategy

- Coordinate Across Live Ops: Gather direction from events and monetization product managers, resolve conflicts across overlapping workstreams, and ensure that individual components reinforce the overall monthly plan

- Improve Operating Systems: Create and refine templates, checklists, documentation, and repeatable workflows that increase implementation speed, reduce errors, and make execution easier to scale

- Use Data to Inform Delivery: Use performance data and player segmentation to understand the intent behind requirements, validate implementation choices, and support post-launch reviews

- Accelerate Through Artificial Intelligence: Use artificial intelligence tools, including Codex and ChatGPT, to develop requirements, analyze data, create documentation, identify inconsistencies, and improve execution quality

What We're Looking For

- 3+ years experience in live operations, product operations, production, product management, or a comparable execution-focused role in mobile or free-to-play games

- A high-ownership, hardworking operating style and a strong desire to grow a career in mobile game product management

- Exceptional organization, follow-through, and attention to detail across multiple concurrent deadlines and workstreams

- Experience translating ambiguous or high-level direction into precise tickets, requirements, and acceptance criteria; familiarity with Jira is strongly preferred

- The judgment to evaluate both configuration accuracy and whether an implementation supports the intended player and business outcomes

- Comfort managing external partners or distributed implementation teams through clear delegation, prioritization, feedback, and escalation

- Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to inform events and monetization requirements; Structured Query Language (SQL) proficiency is preferred

- Demonstrated comfort using artificial intelligence tools to accelerate analysis, documentation, quality assurance, and workflow improvement

- Clear written and verbal communication with product, economy, analytics, production, and implementation partners

Bonus Points

- Hands-on experience with SQL, BigQuery, Looker, or comparable analytics tools

- Experience designing milestone systems, event rewards, or progression-based monetization in a role-playing game or Hero Collector

- A deep understanding of the Marvel intellectual property and its player community

jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Performance Marketing Manager, Forecasting & Market Intelligence, to join our Performance Marketing team in Canada on a remote basis.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day, whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers developing, publishing, and innovating across the games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

The Performance Marketing team helps drive sustainable player growth across Scopely’s portfolio. This role will sit at the intersection of performance marketing, forecasting, competitive intelligence, and market research, supporting active and upcoming Slate titles as they move from early planning through testing, soft launch, and global launch.

What You Will Do

You will build the analytical foundation behind UA forecasts and growth plans: identifying the right comparable titles, developing market and geo assumptions, maintaining benchmarks, tracking competitive signals, and turning incomplete information into structured first-pass recommendations. This is a highly analytical role for someone who enjoys working through ambiguity and can challenge, validate, and refine assumptions rather than taking inputs at face value.

- Develop first-pass performance marketing forecasts and supporting inputs for upcoming Slate titles, including install curves, geo-tier views, channel assumptions, paid and organic assumptions, and launch phasing.

- Build and maintain relevant comparable game-peer sets based on genre, monetization model, platform, geo mix, audience, launch strategy, creative approach, and expected scale.

- Develop and maintain dCPI benchmarks and degradation curves, combining Scopely historical performance, partner benchmarks, competitor data, and external market signals.

- Support organic forecasting by developing assumptions around baseline organic demand, paid-driven lift, launch/IP halo, virality, and organic-to-paid ratios.

- Build sensitivity analyses that make the impact of key assumptions clear and help teams understand the range of potential outcomes.

- Track competitor UA investment, creative trends, app-store movement, channel activity, launch performance, and regional signals across relevant games and genres.

- Produce recurring market-intelligence and competitive-pulse readouts that identify meaningful changes in the market and potential implications for Slate titles.

- Incorporate learnings from market research, beta acquisition, creative and audience testing, soft launch, and other pre-launch signals into forecast assumptions.

- Support regional opportunity sizing and geo strategy, including differences in acquisition cost, scale, organic potential, and market dynamics.

- Maintain clear assumption logs, source documentation, version history, confidence levels, and open questions so forecasts are auditable and reusable.

- Partner closely with Performance Marketing, Product, Strategic Marketing, Finance, Analytics, and other stakeholders to gather inputs and pressure-test assumptions.

- Proactively identify gaps, risks, or inconsistencies in forecasts and surface them before they become downstream planning issues.

- Support ad hoc Slate analyses and leadership requests with structured research, quantitative analysis, and clear first-pass readouts.

- Help improve and standardize forecasting methodologies, benchmark libraries, and analytical processes across Slate over time.

- Strong experience in performance marketing, growth, marketing analytics, strategy, market intelligence, or a similarly analytical role, ideally within mobile games, mobile apps, or another consumer digital business.

- Strong understanding of mobile user acquisition fundamentals, including CPI, LTV, ROAS, retention, organic acquisition, channel mix, attribution, and marginal economics.

- Excellent analytical skills and the ability to turn incomplete or ambiguous information into structured assumptions and useful recommendations.

- Strong Excel / Google Sheets skills, including building and auditing analytical models, sensitivity analyses, and forecast frameworks.

- Strong attention to detail and a high bar for model integrity, source quality, and assumption validation.

- Ability to independently pressure-test data and assumptions rather than accepting outputs at face value.

- Experience working with multiple data sources, including internal performance data, third-party market intelligence tools, partner benchmarks, and competitive research.

- Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Strong cross-functional working style and comfort partnering with teams across Marketing, Product, Finance, Analytics, and leadership.

- Curiosity about the games market and a desire to understand why titles grow, why acquisition economics differ, and how launch dynamics evolve over time.

- Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and operate effectively with limited oversight.

- Comfortable using AI and other analytical tools to accelerate research and analysis, while maintaining independent judgment and thoroughly validating outputs.

Bonus Points

- You are an avid gamer who understands products from a user’s perspective.

- Direct experience forecasting or supporting the launch of mobile games or consumer apps.

- Experience with tools such as Sensor Tower, data.ai, AppMagic, Looker, Appsflyer, Adjust, or similar platforms.

- Familiarity with global mobile UA markets and meaningful differences across the US, Tier 1 Western markets, Asia, and emerging regions.

- Experience analyzing competitor launches, creative strategy, market sizing, or portfolio-level performance.

- Familiarity with pre-launch testing, soft-launch methodology, or forecasting games with licensed or globally recognized IP.

jobs.description:
Scopely  is seeking a Senior Finance Analyst to join the team behind MONOPOLY GO!  This role will be located in Culver City, CA on a hybrid basis.

In this role, you will own the game’s recurring operational finance activities while building the tools and automation that make our work faster, more accurate, and more scalable. MONOPOLY GO! is a global phenomenon and the biggest mobile game launch in history, captivating millions of players worldwide.

You will lead operating expense month-end close, accruals, headcount tracking, purchase orders, Workday approvals, and T&E visibility. This is a build-oriented role with a clear mandate to improve how the work gets done—not simply execute existing processes. We are looking for someone who can identify opportunities to apply AI and automation thoughtfully and effectively.

Over time, this role will help advance an AI-native approach to FP&A, connecting close, planning, reporting, and approvals so routine work can run more efficiently and the team can focus on higher-value judgment. This is a greenfield opportunity with significant autonomy and a dedicated budget for tools and experimentation.

You will also serve as the primary Finance business partner to our Engineering organization, acting as its main point of contact for spending, headcount, and planning. You will work closely with Finance Managers, the VP of Finance for MONOPOLY GO!, and cross-functional partners across the business, with strong senior-level support as you ramp into the role.

Why this role stands out

- A build mandate. You own the FP&A automation stack — greenfield, with autonomy and a tool budget. A real part of the job is making the work better, not only keeping it running.

- Scale and visibility. MONOPOLY GO! is a large, fast-growing business. Your work informs game leadership directly, with regular exposure to the VP of Finance.

- Room to grow. A path into complex modeling, financial storytelling, and broader scope across Scopely's portfolio, with mentorship to get there.

- A strong team. You'll join a high-caliber group with backgrounds across high-growth tech, consulting, banking, and private equity.

What you'll do

The split is honest: expect the operational cadence to be a meaningful part of your week, and the build work to grow as you automate more of it.

- Run the OpEx close cadence. Month-end close, accruals, reclasses, and headcount reconciliation, plus high-volume PO/Workday approvals and T&E — accurately, on time, and independently before long.

- Build the automation. Replace manual reporting with automated workflows and dashboards, and apply AI where it genuinely helps across close, planning, reporting, and approvals.

- Partner with Engineering. Act as the finance business partner to the MONOPOLY GO! Engineering organization — helping them understand and plan their spend and headcount — and work with People & Talent, Business Operations, Customer Support, and QA to gather budget inputs and explain OpEx variances clearly.

- Think in systems. Connect steps across finance so the process gets simpler over time, with sensible checks where judgment matters.

- Keep the models trustworthy. Maintain revenue/cost and workforce-planning models so leadership sees current, reconciled, defensible numbers.

What we're looking for

- An automation habit — you've automated manual reporting or finance processes, and you're interested in applying AI to real work. Experience with BigQuery, SQL, Python, or AI tools is a big plus

- Operational reliability — a track record of dependable, detail-accurate delivery on recurring, high-volume work

- Clear communication — you can explain numbers and variances to non-finance partners

- Located in, or willing to relocate to, the Los Angeles metro, working on-site/hybrid

- Ownership and integrity — you do well in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, and are always looking for ways to add value

- Strong Excel and financial modeling — you build and maintain revenue/cost models and handle large datasets without hand-holding

- Hands-on FP&A foundation — you've done planning, forecasting, variance analysis, and a real close/reporting cadence, and can hit the ground running

- 2–5 years of finance/analytical experience, ideally in FP&A or finance at a brand-name technology or high-growth company

How you work

- You form your own point of view and make the case for it — and you let it go gracefully when someone has the better argument.

- You lead with questions. You learn why something is the way it is before you start rewiring it.

- You get to great by iterating. You put a solid version out early, invite feedback, and keep sharpening it.

- When something falls between the cracks, you assume it's yours. You close the loop instead of flagging it and moving on.

- When you hit the same manual task twice, your instinct is to automate it — not grind through it a third time.

Nice to have

- An undergraduate degree in engineering (computer, mechanical, electrical, industrial, aerospace, etc.) — a real plus for this role.

- Something you've built — an automation or tool you can walk us through.

- Experience with financial systems such as Oracle and Workday / Workday Adaptive Planning.

- Data platforms — Big Query, etc.

- A genuine interest in games, consumer products, or technology-driven businesses.
